text:
support-ops: FYI customers reporting sudden spike in 502/504s to hosted inference since the canary rollout at 08:09 UTC. Multiple tickets coming in.
alex: which canary and which config changed? any recent flag flips?
deploy-bot: Started canary rollout commit abc123 at 08:09 UTC. Variant tag: canary-prefetch-v2. Config overrides: prefetch_enabled=true, prefetch_window_ms=0, batching_mode=adaptive.
maria: seeing gateway timeouts to runtime, upstream timeouts cluster-wide in the canary tag. Error rate went from ~0.2% to 8% in 3 minutes.
maria: sample router log snippet:
```
[08:13:02] router.go:215 upstream error status=504 err=upstream timeout route=/v1/generate tag=canary-prefetch-v2
[08:13:05] router.go:215 upstream error status=502 err=bad gateway route=/v1/embeddings tag=canary-prefetch-v2
```
sam: prefetch_window_ms=0 is suspicious. That effectively disables prefix prefetch and might change batching behavior. If runtime expects KV cache priming, cold paths could blow up latency and hit timeouts.
priya: also seeing a surge of 429s from runtime + then 504s at the gateway. Could be a throttling / shedder interaction.
alex: any recent kernel/channel changes on runtime?
maria: no runtime deploys in last hour, only this canary config change. Telemetry shows per-request processing time for canary backends spiking to 11s for many calls. SLO is 5s.
sam: propose immediate traffic cut for canary and rollback config. Two-step: 1) route 100% traffic to stable, 2) rollback config override.
priya: warning — previous partial rollback attempt yesterday caused a routing race where some frontend shards still saw the flag for a few minutes and doubled errors during the transition. We should coordinate shard drain.
alex: agree. Steps:
1) set routing weight canary 0% via control plane
2) wait for in-flight to drain (60s) and watch error rate
3) revert config on canary hosts or clear override
4) scale stable up by 10% if needed
5) monitor 5xx and latency

maria: I'm running the rollback now, starting with step 1. Executing router weight update.
deploy-bot: routing update accepted. canary-prefetch-v2 weight set to 0 at 08:17:12 UTC.
maria: draining in-flight now. currently observing slow drop in errors but still seeing tails.
sam: running quick check on kvcache metrics. kvcache miss rate shot up to 96% on canary. Looks like prefetch disabled caused mass misses.
priya: going to revert the override on the canary hosts. I'll push config revert patch and patch rollout token.
priya: revert applied at 08:18:30 UTC.
maria: confirm patch landed, but some frontends still have flag in memory. K8s rollout on canary pods will take a bit.
alex: to prevent the race, we should also patch routing table to avoid sending any new requests to canary and then trigger a pod restart sequence.
priya: restarting canary pods now one by one.
ops-bot: Incident created #incident-1764543210 at 08:19 UTC. Paging oncall SRE.
maria: error rate falling to ~0.8% now. Latency back to normal on stable.
sam: recommend follow-up postmortem: include a canary checklist for flag changes that impact kvcache/prefetch and an automated gating rule that blocks prefetch_window_ms=0 during rolling canaries.
alex: agreed. Support-ops, please update affected customer tickets with mitigation steps and ETA for full recovery.
support-ops: Marking P0. Updating customers: we rolled back canary config and drained traffic, errors are subsiding. Will update once all canary pods restarted and metrics stable for 15m.
maria: final check at 08:28:45 UTC — 5xx rate for platform has returned to baseline. Closing immediate mitigation.
support-ops: thanks all. Creating follow-up runbook issue for canary flag gating and adding a note to deploy guide.
priya: will open PR with gating rule and test in sandbox tomorrow.
alex: good job, team.
